DeanNoriko said:
Some very quick first thoughts regarding the new update:

Ayane from a timeline where her feelings are not being reciprocated by Akira is very cute. Not that I don't like "our" Ayane, but it was refreshing and heartwarming.
View attachment 4190528 View attachment 4190529 View attachment 4190531 View attachment 4190532
This whole timeline (apart from Ayane) was just really creepy. I hated Sekai and it immediately destroyed all benefit of doubt I gave her during last update's Kyoto scene. She really was just a horrible abuser, it seems. Unless there has been some godfuckery involved to make her this way. Also, apparently we have a confirmation that Akira is Ami's Dad. Although I find it suspicious how Nozumu has been conveniently left out during this whole sharade. View attachment 4190539
Holy Maya Macaroni, I really hate this Akira. I will have to assume this is the creepy ass version of Akira from most of the other timelines that has been hinted at by Maya and Yumi, because the way he talks to Maya and the way he looks at her is really just giving me "I'm a piece of shit abuser and I like it" vibe, in contrast to the "I'm a piece of shit abuser but I hate myself for it and am a depressed mess as a result" vibe he has going on in "our" timeline. View attachment 4190551
Oh yes, as a Karin stan I was not only pumped to see her in that hot Wii Fit outfit, we even learn she is basically the closest to a LI after Ami in this reality, LETSGO. Ironically mostly because somehow Akira is really into football which I inexplicably found really funny. barglenarglezous Given Sel is American, I am 99% sure he was referring to American football, he would use soccer specifically if he were to refer to that sport. He has been using that term during the many soccer practice events with Miku, Karin and Kirin.
View attachment 4190571
I'm really curious how new Nodoka will change going forward. I suppose it is implied that she will not retain most of the crucial memories that brought her into the position she found herself in, so I wonder how much she will really know and try to find out and how Akira plans to stop her (assuming he will remember to do so, which is also implied at the end of the update).
View attachment 4190580
During this scene it is implied that Ayane knows for certain that Yumi and Akira did not have sex, which obviously refers to the list she made Akira do with all the girls he screwed. Was that not supposed to be a retained memory of Ayane's? Why would that particular information be deleted? View attachment 4190585
I was also very happy to see that one of my biggest gripes about Maya's lore has been addressed (see one of my previous posts ) where I protested that Maya would be unable to retain anywhere near the amount of memory that she claimed she had lived through. Now either Sel is reading along here (in which case, Hi!) or he has just naturally come to the conclusion that it needs to be explained, which would also give Maya's boxes a potential purpose, so he might have had that in mind the whole time. View attachment 4190640

Also, needless to say, the reset puzzle was dog shit. I don't know what I expected. I guess, after Sensei Quest, for him to become a bit more creative. This just felt like a drag and I would have taken way too long for me to come up with all of the answers on my own accord. I've lost all hope of him producing any good and interesting reset puzzles.
Click to expand...
1. Innocent Ayane is so cute, I agree. It's interesting how that must have been sort of the original Ayane, the one Akira refused to act towards in a romantic sense.

2. And yes, I think no one commented on it, but the version of Sekai that got married to Akira after Kyoto really hammers how she is a predator through and through. She seems controlled by Akira, only going after the ones he wants her to, but still. Glad we got that sorted - as Sekai being only attracted to Akira (in terms of predation) was a possibility for a while. Doesn't seem so anymore, and she certainly considers having Ami take part of it something desirable.

3. I think aramaug has touched on the point of who this Akira is, and it wasn't an Akira at all apparently, being rather the same person that she recognizes as not being him in the tutoring flashback. Maybe Ami? I don't know.

4. Karin cucking Ami by being a "bro chick" is so funny though lol but also, I think, very accurate to when she comes to see Akira after his assault. The underlying message of that whole conversation is that Karin would have been okay with it if he loved her and if she was the only one which, in that reality, seems to be the case. Go Karin.

5. I think she's dead/no memories will carry over. I have commented on this already, but man, kudos to Selebus cause I have a real hard time in seeing Nodoka as a villain now. Not only I got her already through these last updates, but her literal sacrifice so that Akira could see firsthand Ami being a psychopath kind of redeemed her enough in my eyes that I can at the very least be neutral toward her. Who knew.

6. I'm very curious about Himawari's background. Because putting things together, she was cared for as a baby by Akira (arms bent back), then she went back into Alexis' belly and was there until she was Himawari's age/appearance as we know it now? Thing's so confusing.

7. Also confused about that. Maybe she was losing those memories because they weren't coherent with the timeline she was in? When she comes back to our timeline she has issues with it being Spring, instead calling it Winter (spring is the opposite in this case, a thing that wouldn't have existed in Alt Maya's timeline).

8. And likely explained the boxes at the same time. I think Selebus did say at one point that the boxes weren't going to be that amazing in the first place. And well, Maya's diaries certainly fit the bill (they make sense though).

spoilers.title: reply
spoilers.html:
1. Innocent Ayane is so cute, I agree. It's interesting how that must have been sort of the original Ayane, the one Akira refused to act towards in a romantic sense.

2. And yes, I think no one commented on it, but the version of Sekai that got married to Akira after Kyoto really hammers how she is a predator through and through. She seems controlled by Akira, only going after the ones he wants her to, but still. Glad we got that sorted - as Sekai being only attracted to Akira (in terms of predation) was a possibility for a while. Doesn't seem so anymore, and she certainly considers having Ami take part of it something desirable.

3. I think aramaug has touched on the point of who this Akira is, and it wasn't an Akira at all apparently, being rather the same person that she recognizes as not being him in the tutoring flashback. Maybe Ami? I don't know.

4. Karin cucking Ami by being a "bro chick" is so funny though lol but also, I think, very accurate to when she comes to see Akira after his assault. The underlying message of that whole conversation is that Karin would have been okay with it if he loved her and if she was the only one which, in that reality, seems to be the case. Go Karin.

5. I think she's dead/no memories will carry over. I have commented on this already, but man, kudos to Selebus cause I have a real hard time in seeing Nodoka as a villain now. Not only I got her already through these last updates, but her literal sacrifice so that Akira could see firsthand Ami being a psychopath kind of redeemed her enough in my eyes that I can at the very least be neutral toward her. Who knew.

6. I'm very curious about Himawari's background. Because putting things together, she was cared for as a baby by Akira (arms bent back), then she went back into Alexis' belly and was there until she was Himawari's age/appearance as we know it now? Thing's so confusing.

7. Also confused about that. Maybe she was losing those memories because they weren't coherent with the timeline she was in? When she comes back to our timeline she has issues with it being Spring, instead calling it Winter (spring is the opposite in this case, a thing that wouldn't have existed in Alt Maya's timeline).

8. And likely explained the boxes at the same time. I think Selebus did say at one point that the boxes weren't going to be that amazing in the first place. And well, Maya's diaries certainly fit the bill (they make sense though).

Moonflare said:
8. And likely explained the boxes at the same time. I think Selebus did say at one point that the boxes weren't going to be that amazing in the first place. And well, Maya's diaries certainly fit the bill (they make sense though).[/SPOILER]
Click to expand...
I still have faith that there's something more interesting going on with the boxes, even though journals/notes make sense.
  • Selebus has been building up the boxes for a long time, including teasing them repeatedly in every recent update. I can't see him doing a "reveal" where we never see a box and the only thing we're told about the contents is that Ayane didn't learn a single useful/interesting thing from them.
  • The alt timeline Maya says that she keeps her notes in the basement, but Maya Prime always had Sensei deliver the boxes to one particular room on the third floor, which we still have never seen inside of. The room has to be important somehow.
To digress a bit, I'm a bit annoyed by Ayane's timeline because it just feels kind of pointless. Sel effectively brings Maya Prime back from the dead and then doesn't have her say or do anything interesting. We learn she keeps notes, but they're useless. Maya and Ayane spend a lot of time talking about their feelings for each other, but that was just putting into words what was effectively shown by their interactions in Chapter 3; and in the end, Ayane forgets everything, so it's not like her own understanding of their relationship progressed at all. They conspicuously don't talk about anything actually important - is it really plausible that Ayane never asks Maya how she resets the world? How about anything about Maya's past - she gives Ayane the scarf to gain New Maya's trust, but wouldn't information be a lot more effective?

I still have faith that there's something more interesting going on with the boxes, even though journals/notes make sense.
  • Selebus has been building up the boxes for a long time, including teasing them repeatedly in every recent update. I can't see him doing a "reveal" where we never see a box and the only thing we're told about the contents is that Ayane didn't learn a single useful/interesting thing from them.
  • The alt timeline Maya says that she keeps her notes in the basement, but Maya Prime always had Sensei deliver the boxes to one particular room on the third floor, which we still have never seen inside of. The room has to be important somehow.
To digress a bit, I'm a bit annoyed by Ayane's timeline because it just feels kind of pointless. Sel effectively brings Maya Prime back from the dead and then doesn't have her say or do anything interesting. We learn she keeps notes, but they're useless. Maya and Ayane spend a lot of time talking about their feelings for each other, but that was just putting into words what was effectively shown by their interactions in Chapter 3; and in the end, Ayane forgets everything, so it's not like her own understanding of their relationship progressed at all. They conspicuously don't talk about anything actually important - is it really plausible that Ayane never asks Maya how she resets the world? How about anything about Maya's past - she gives Ayane the scarf to gain New Maya's trust, but wouldn't information be a lot more effective?

Something interesting that I don't think has gained much notice is that it was again implied that even Sensei being aware of the Resets isn't relatively normal in the Resets.

In Ayane's Chapter 4 'Chamomile' Event, the Alt Maya Prime reveals:
Alt Maya Prime - "No...I've been here the whole time. My last reset was months ago. But nobody else is supposed to know about them here."
Ayane - "Not even Sensei?"
Alt Maya Prime - "Definitely not Sensei. He's too busy fucking Ami to figure any of that stuff out. And I doubt he'll-"
- "Wait..."
- "Was that you...implying he actually figures it out in your timeline? Or...is that just wishful thinking on my end?"
That in her world (Football Sensei), she is the only one who knows about the Resets. Her Sensei doesn't and it seems like her Ami probably doesn't either (or at least this Maya implies that), and it seems like none of the previous Senseis had figured it out in this world either.

Our Maya Prime actually had also implied that Sensei being aware of Resets was a new thing:
Maya Prime - "Until recently, I was the only one whose memories carried over from loop to loop. But changes made to the formula of this for unknown reasons have now landed both Ayane and Sensei beside me."
(Chapter 3 Makoto 'Suffer the Same' Event)
So, something probably happened before our Sensei showed up that made it possible for Sensei to make it to the roof and become aware of things. (Our Maya Prime didn't seem surprised that our Sensei knew of the Resets so it probably happened before Chapter 1)

I'm thinking a certain Shapeshifter, may have been behind that:
Himawari - "In many respects, I'm just as lost as you are."
(Chapter 3 Sana 'Ad Meliora' Event)
Her presumed father and mother both becoming aware of the Resets, one after another, seems suspicious.

There's also how Himawari was involved in our Sensei buying the Scarf that he gives to our Maya Prime, who seemed to not have had that Scarf:

added numbers for clarity.
1. Maya not being aware of Ami being aware of the reset might just be an aftereffect of Maya Prime being unaware of it. That was not the best way to put it. I mean that a prior Maya to Maya Prime might have been aware of Ami being "awake", but this Maya (Prime or alt) isn't.

In her perception, Ami starts acting "crazy" when she starts to notice something is wrong. But that could easily just be the case that Ami drops the facade when she assumes that the current cycle is not interesting to her anymore - and why would she communicate that to Maya in the first place? She might be wanting to keep Maya in the dark about her as well for some reason. There's definitely something going on because for all of the cycles and times Maya Prime has made it through the resets (and Ami going insane), in not a single one of them Ami killed Maya. That's just beyond suspicious.

So maybe Ami isn't killing Maya on purpose, maybe cause she knows it leads nowhere (from having done it so many times) and is on a sort of "Sensei situation", where Maya factory reset Akira so many times by fucking him that she keeps her distance now. Maybe Ami is also avoiding "bringing Maya into the fold", or rather having yet another awake Maya that doesn't know anything, and instead chooses to keep the one that brings Akira up to speed by herself.

This is all a shot in the dark by this point.

2. But back to theorizing, I thought that Maya Prime was simply surprised because it was the same scarf, but that the original scarf was still in her possession, just hidden away (as alt Maya says). I find it extremely doubtful that Maya would throw away the scarf in the first place. I think that's an easier answer, and that after receiving the scarf she might have went back to check if the original was still in the basement.

It's possible that it is a paradox situation though, didn't think about that.

3. I mean, Noriko already drugged Akira. Which we often forget from how much pity we have for her. Really not okay and if anything that would be an instant deal breaker for me for at least for forever.

Do any of you think we may have reached a Death of the Author situation already with this game?

Have we/you, constantly crafting theories by trying to guess where Sel is taking the story, possibly created an interpretation we consider to be superior than Sel's original intent? I think it's important to note that while Sel writes with good prose, it's not necessarily given that he's a great author nor story creator. I'm not saying he isn't, but I think it's important to remember he's just one person, who is fallible, and is literally writing a story on a month-to-month basis, where any number of decisions can be made that change the plot trajectory based on his whims.

I'm just curious to see if anyone else thinks we may have reached a point where our interpretation of the story and its symbolism exceeds that which Sel wrote it with.

Guys my understanding is that Death of the Author (DoA) is about ignoring the author's "original intent" when analyzing a work's themes:
  • DoA is not about going off and writing your own fanfic/ending/continuation because that has nothing to do with the literary/thematic analysis of a work
  • DoA is totally orthogonal to the lore of the world because that lore is for the most part just a matter of facts, e.g. there's not much room for subjective interpretation on the matter of "is Nozomu Akira's brother?" And although we can spend lots of time arguing about whether Yuu is Akira's dad or grandpa, it is mostly inconsequential from the perspective of analysis
  • DoA is totally orthogonal to the completion state of the work because that has no bearing on the themes present within the work as it is available for consumption right now, today
    • You could say that the themes may not be explored as fully as the author had intended. But DoA is about disregarding the author's intent so whether a given theme has been fleshed out and conveyed as the author had intended is irrelevant

That's a very interesting point that you are making and something I have been thinking about a few times.

First off, I very highly doubt that Sel is really taking into consideration fan theories, neither on Lilcord nor (and especially so) here. Anyone reading his responses in the Ask-Selebus channel will notice that he has near zero concern about what kind of ideas and suggestions the community has in terms of the overall story. He is very confident in his abilities and will follow his own guidance, rather than find inspiration from his "subjects/patrons".

Secondly, he repeatedly said that the general plot is already set in stone, and only details are up to discussion. For example, the general ending is decided as well as the overall theme for the dark path, but the individual purity paths he has not thought out yet for every character, which is understandable to be honest.
I also have the feeling, especially now that I am replaying this game for the first time, that he did have a vision from the very start, certain elements he had in mind that would come into action much later on, being hinted at subtly throughout the game. So I do have faith in him that he is able to connect all of the dots and have answers for most, if not all, of the open questions within the story.

That being said, there is always the danger that some of those decisions may backfire or turn out not as well thought through as he initially anticipated. He is a human after all, he is not immune to mistakes. For example, I am still not 100% sure whether this whole Noriko age thing from Kyoto is intended and another mystery in itself or just a brain fart from his side (this has been discussed already, so I'm not intending to re-heat this point, just giving it as an example).

Many giga brain chads on here have given very plausible and interesting theories that might realistically be even better than what Sel initially thought of, sure. A hivemind of creative and intelligent people can probably come up with a few very good ideas that might surpass the original vision. However, I trust the author to follow his vision, to fit everything as they intended it to. And even if it does not turn out to be perfect, Sel has not given me enough reason to doubt him to deliver a satisfying wrap-up of the general story points.

It's probably just good advice in general to not get expectation unreasonably high, you can't satisfy everyone and there will be certain aspects that some might find more problematic than others (e.g. that whole NTR thing). But I personally think that his track record so far shows that he is a capable enough writer to not disappoint us too much in the end. Or so I hope.

Too many posts to reply to, so I won't quote anyone - just feel as if I have. This is about the death of the author.

I agree that it is hard to apply the concept of the death of the author (basically the idea that after a piece of work is done, no longer the say of what it means lies with the author, but rather with the reader - as it assumes that the meaning of a piece of literature is built through the collaboration of both author and reader, and that any author will touch unforeseen themes with their work that are still valid despite their intentions) to an ongoing story.

The second issue is that the death of the author isn't really meant to be used (or rather often used) for objective things within a narrative. Rather, it is used to discuss interpretations of the evidence presented, or of things left unexplained. In LiL's case, we just haven't been presented with the full picture yet. Which, again, is why formal literature guidelines aren't supportive of the publishing (and even less of the reviews) of ongoing works.

What I think we're doing, and similar to the criticism of Rowling's 6th book, is that as LiL continues, we become able to pinpoint, with increasing substance, areas where Selebus fell short (or rather seems to have fallen short). I, myself, have often wondered if by the end of all of this a substantial amount of lore wouldn't be just derivative misdirection made on the fly.

Back to Rowling, I do think she's a wonderful writer, it's just that being a wonderful writer can mean a number of things. She was able to capitalize on so much of actual myths, traditions and essence (and frustration) of the coming of age narrative and turn it into an astounding success. To not call that wonderful writing (at the very least in worldbuilding/and or understanding her target audience) would be unfair.

Both My Hero Academia and Dragonball are part of generational shounen, though dragon ball is two times removed from the current (?) generation (which includes My Hero). I don't know that I'd call anything there genius, but they're the big names within their own genre. I wouldn't go looking for "high" literature in a shonen in the first place, it follows that we would judge the literature within a genre by their own indicators - unless it somehow subverts or escapes it, like, it could be said, of Attack on Titan.

All in all, I think we have to wait for Selebus to release the equivalent of his "6th book", which would likely be the first purity route, to have proper early conclusions. If Himawari's name isn't Ami/Amy it's all obviously a piece of shit and he changed it just to spite me though.

Guys my understanding is that Death of the Author (DoA) is about ignoring the author's "original intent" when analyzing a work's themes:
  • DoA is not about going off and writing your own fanfic/ending/continuation because that has nothing to do with the literary/thematic analysis of a work
  • DoA is totally orthogonal to the lore of the world because that lore is for the most part just a matter of facts, e.g. there's not much room for subjective interpretation on the matter of "is Nozomu Akira's brother?" And although we can spend lots of time arguing about whether Yuu is Akira's dad or grandpa, it is mostly inconsequential from the perspective of analysis
  • DoA is totally orthogonal to the completion state of the work because that has no bearing on the themes present within the work as it is available for consumption right now, today
    • You could say that the themes may not be explored as fully as the author had intended. But DoA is about disregarding the author's intent so whether a given theme has been fleshed out and conveyed as the author had intended is irrelevant

I haven't finished because I hit a rare bug that made me unable to interact with statues and chests (and Solas' memories because of that). So I'm waiting around for a fix which is a huge bummer.
I think veilguard lacked better direction. Combat is fine, but I just set it to the easiest cause it started to felt spongy after a while. Environments look great, enemies look from generic to ridiculous. Overall story is okay, but could have been presented better, especially the beginning (people say the ending is amazing, but I haven't reached it unfortunately).

The pacing between main quest and companion quests is bad (eventually they just dump 20 quests on you on the final stretch - mass effect 2 did it much better). The companion quests I have finished (just Bellara's) was a great setup that ended up being lackluster for me.

Main issue I have is the dialogue. Everything is sanitized, you have three different ways of being supportive of your companions no matter what, you either agree with how Rook handles every situation or too bad. The worst of it all is Taash's questline, not because it's about being non-binary (although I agree that it's tackled in a weird way), but because the character itself ranges from a bizarre self-insert to the most confrontational character in the series, they're hostile to you, to companions, to their family, and yet all Rook can be is supportive no matter what. As someone that is supportive and has been supportive of non-binary people in real life (not on the internet either), and other minorities, I genuinely thought that it was a disservice to the people I've met, that behave like actual people and are generally pleasant to be around, instead of whatever that "angsty teenager I can be rude to everyone cause I have identity issues and they'll give me a pass for it" is supposed to be.

I go hard on this because, again, it's the culmination of the main problem with the game, lack of direction in how to present dialogue and questlines. Inquisition had a trans character and did an awesome portrayal of a gay man that was reviled by his family for it. Moonflare said:
Edit: if the question is about the series, then it's a great series. I like it. Although it is weird that every game kind of tried to reinvent itself.
Click to expand...
When you look into the circumstances behind each game, this trend makes a lot more sense.

When BioWare lost the D&D license, they really wanted to continue making high fantasy RPGs, so they set about making their own world. Because they wanted to hurry up and get to the fun part (actually making the game) they spedrun the world building, which is why demons are literally just the 7 deadly sins, the spirits are just the 7 cardinal virues, the original presentation of Daelish was Native American-coded, the original Qunari were Muslim coded, etc). Then they spent a LONG time on the game itself, including building a propietary engine.

The game did well, and so did the expansion, so EA gave them 13 months to make a sequel. This is a VERY short turnaround for BioWare, which is why the story feels more like 3 chapters pulled randomly from an anthology with little in-between connective tissue and side quests are pulled from 4-5 recycled environments. They had to cut a lot of corners to make the deadline.

When they started on Inquisition, open world was taking off, so EA imposed an open-world requirement on them, and the existing engine didn't accomodate an expansive open world, so they had to change engines and playstyle -- only for the biggest complaint about the game to be the expansive open world and how it was implemented.

They then began work on Dread Wolf.

Midway through Dread Wolf's development, EA imposed a Live Service requirement on the game, so everything they had at the time was largely tossed, and the game restarted. Veteran DA designers began jumping ship. By the time EA retracted the Live Service requirement (which prompted another "toss what we have and start over") there was no longer anyone left at BioWare who even knew how to code for the Origins/2 engine, making a remaster of the original games impossible (which is why we'll never see a trilogy release like Mass Effect got). The final game was literally the 3rd attempt at making a follow up to Inquisition to be started at BioWare. Lead directors changed twice over, I believe. Most of the people working on it were actually from the Mass Effect team, not the Dragon Age team, which is why the quest structure feels much more Mass Effect 2 than any Dragon Age has ever been. And after 10 years in development, EA urged them to finish the game as a complete product, not plan for any DLC, and after a patch-fix post-release period, the team will begin workiing on the next Mass Effect in earnest. So it feels rushed because it WAS rushed. Two false starts and an impatient publisher will do that. The game winds up sharing a lot of the circumstances that Dragon Age 2 had as a result, and it's getting a lot of the same complaints that people had with Dragon Age 2 back when it came out. What a coincidence.

After platinuming the game, it was enjoyable and satisfyinig. It's not a game of the year, but it's definitely in my top 5 for new releases I played this year.

If anyone case, that top 5 is:
1) Persona 3 Reload
2) Final Fantasy VII Rebirth
3) Veilguard
4) Mechwarrior 5: The Clans
5) Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance

Notes: I haven't played Metaphor Refantazio yet, but everything I've seen tells me it'd wind up on this list, and SMTV is only as low as it is because I wasn't in the right headspace for that kind of game when I played it, and will go back when I'm in the mood for it. If any of these games is falling off to make room for Metaphor, it'll probably be MechWarrior.

For anyone who is in the same boat as me and can't contribute much to the ongoing off-topic discussions (this is not criticism btw, if anything then it's just me admitting to be boring), here's a few more thoughts I had during my continued replay of the game. And I apologize in case some of those thing have already been mentioned or discussed in the past, since this is gonna be some really old stuff.


It would be ironic if Maya and possibly Yumi would turn out to be the only constant gf's Akira had in previous timelines.

Poor Osako (also eww the hair)

Himawari would like to have a word with you.


Well...
There was a few things I really tried to pay attention to, but with what we learned in the most recent updates, maybe the most glaring thing for me is to really take a close look at Ami.
And I must say, there is really zero signs that she would be this omnipresent being that has a wicked and twisted plan and who wants to manipulate the world into something else. I'm not saying it's not possible, but at least before the first reset, Ami seems very innocent (in comparison) and I didn't notice any hints of her being Prime Ami or having any extra knowledge. This might of course change in the future chapters.
However, one thing from the very beginning made me wonder. Where was the journal from? The one Akira allegedly just kept in his room prior to the very first reset. I feel like this has been addressed before, and there might be an explanation coming where Maya might have actually left it for him, similar to the notes on the board. But just in case it is not, that very entry here would simply not make sense:
If this was written by pre-reset Akira, he would not actually think that, obviously. Unless he was so paranoid that he was even afraid someone might go through his personal notes at home and find evidence of him having an affair with a student. Come to think of it, I guess it could be in character? Still, feels like a convenient lie to basically hide the plot twist for later.
So the first time I played this game, it must have been somewhere around update 0.13 to 0.16 or something. I didn't actually quit after the first happy scene or anything else disturbing like apparently so many players do. Admittedly though this game gave me this unique uneasiness that was both fascinating but also distracting.

The thing is, playing through the beginning, it reminded me how different I approached it back then. Sure, it was quite clearly intended to be (or at least appear as) a harem parody of sorts, with some DDLC inspirations thrown in for the horror and shock factor. Big fucking whoop. It was still a porn game, so I played it to grind the lewd scenes and "conquer" the girls.
Characters like, for example, Chika or Ayane were great, since they were very open quickly and just really cute and likable. spoilers.title: Now to what really hit me by surprise the most...
spoilers.html:
So the first time I played this game, it must have been somewhere around update 0.13 to 0.16 or something. I didn't actually quit after the first happy scene or anything else disturbing like apparently so many players do. Admittedly though this game gave me this unique uneasiness that was both fascinating but also distracting.

The thing is, playing through the beginning, it reminded me how different I approached it back then. Sure, it was quite clearly intended to be (or at least appear as) a harem parody of sorts, with some DDLC inspirations thrown in for the horror and shock factor. Big fucking whoop. It was still a porn game, so I played it to grind the lewd scenes and "conquer" the girls.
Characters like, for example, Chika or Ayane were great, since they were very open quickly and just really cute and likable. But in the end, I didn't really expect to care for them (much like Sensei then, who openly identified himself as a detached character anyway, especially during the first cycle).

But now, whenever a lewd scene is coming up, I feel like I'm watching a sex scene in a Tom Cruise movie with my parents. Like, whipping out my mole rat to that would straight up feel like I should be put into an asylum. Not that the scenes are not hot or anything per se. It's just that the added context makes me realize that now I am not playing it for any dumb sex scenes anymore, but for the plot. And getting turned on by intimate encounters and character growth just feels so dirty and degenerate to my now all of a sudden.

But I don't know, this might also just be me. And I'm not judging anyone reacting differently to it, I just wanted to highlight the difference in perspective I have apparently grown over the years, with how closely I follow every character's arcs and actually started to see them as people and not CGs to collect. How ironically fitting for the theme, well done Selly.

And I apologize in case some of those thing have already been mentioned or discussed in the past, since this is gonna be some really old stuff.

View attachment 4230525 View attachment 4230526 View attachment 4230528
It would be ironic if Maya and possibly Yumi would turn out to be the only constant gf's Akira had in previous timelines.
View attachment 4230531
Poor Osako (also eww the hair)
View attachment 4230534
Himawari would like to have a word with you.

View attachment 4230536
Well...
There was a few things I really tried to pay attention to, but with what we learned in the most recent updates, maybe the most glaring thing for me is to really take a close look at Ami.
And I must say, there is really zero signs that she would be this omnipresent being that has a wicked and twisted plan and who wants to manipulate the world into something else. I'm not saying it's not possible, but at least before the first reset, Ami seems very innocent (in comparison) and I didn't notice any hints of her being Prime Ami or having any extra knowledge. This might of course change in the future chapters.
However, one thing from the very beginning made me wonder. Where was the journal from? The one Akira allegedly just kept in his room prior to the very first reset. I feel like this has been addressed before, and there might be an explanation coming where Maya might have actually left it for him, similar to the notes on the board. But just in case it is not, that very entry here would simply not make sense:
View attachment 4230548 If this was written by pre-reset Akira, he would not actually think that, obviously. Unless he was so paranoid that he was even afraid someone might go through his personal notes at home and find evidence of him having an affair with a student. Come to think of it, I guess it could be in character? Still, feels like a convenient lie to basically hide the plot twist for later.
So the first time I played this game, it must have been somewhere around update 0.13 to 0.16 or something. I didn't actually quit after the first happy scene or anything else disturbing like apparently so many players do. Admittedly though this game gave me this unique uneasiness that was both fascinating but also distracting.

The thing is, playing through the beginning, it reminded me how different I approached it back then. Sure, it was quite clearly intended to be (or at least appear as) a harem parody of sorts, with some DDLC inspirations thrown in for the horror and shock factor. Big fucking whoop. It was still a porn game, so I played it to grind the lewd scenes and "conquer" the girls.
Characters like, for example, Chika or Ayane were great, since they were very open quickly and just really cute and likable. But in the end, I didn't really expect to care for them (much like Sensei then, who openly identified himself as a detached character anyway, especially during the first cycle).

But now, whenever a lewd scene is coming up, I feel like I'm watching a sex scene in a Tom Cruise movie with my parents. Like, whipping out my mole rat to that would straight up feel like I should be put into an asylum. Not that the scenes are not hot or anything per se. It's just that the added context makes me realize that now I am not playing it for any dumb sex scenes anymore, but for the plot. And getting turned on by intimate encounters and character growth just feels so dirty and degenerate to my now all of a sudden.

But I don't know, this might also just be me. And I'm not judging anyone reacting differently to it, I just wanted to highlight the difference in perspective I have apparently grown over the years, with how closely I follow every character's arcs and actually started to see them as people and not CGs to collect. How ironically fitting for the theme, well done Selly.
So I remember vividly that the last version I had before I paused the game for a long time was 0.21. I actually didn't even finish it, it must have been somewhere in Chapter 2, even before Touka and Yasu joined the class.
That fact turned out to be significant, since I just now found out that there has been a excessive revamp of chapter 1 with the 0.24 update, not only changing a lot of the events but also adding some, notably for example Ode to a Marsh Warbler. I thought I was going crazy, because while I wasn't really surprised to have forgotten a few of the stuff from when I played the game for the first time all those years ago, I was absolutely sure that some stuff just didn't go the way I saw it now, I had to cross check it with the wiki.
It also made me feel less like a big dumb dumb, since it explained some instances where discussions on here were about facts and scenes that I had in mind differently because of it.

Anyways, since the wiki for the Marshwarbler event didn't have the hexadecimal translation for the transition image in the scene, I went ahead and did it myself.
View attachment 4230620

Now I am pretty sure this is just Sel being an ass and insulting me for wasting my time to find answers or hints. But there's enough subtle details in the text where I could at least imagine there might still be some meaning to it.

First off, the background mentions the Daddy Daughter Dance. We now basically have the confirmation that Akira is most likely Ami's Dad, not sure if this was supposed to be some light foreshadowing. But there is also a single blue iris. Who else has a single blue iris? Sel's favourite character, Kaori.
And the text itself mentions a dying cat (cat always makes me think of Maya). But who knits curtains to keep away the shadows? And the rain makes me think of the rain king of course. Is this somehow related to the upside down house?

I am clearly too dumb for this and this probably means nothing. I just had to vent since it took me like 15 minutes to copy all those dumb hexadecimal numbers into the browser
Click to expand...
You're clearly not "too dumb for this"--your instincts and analysis are all spot on.

The thing with all the breadcrumbs Sel has scattered to the wind for us to chase is that it's really easy to start finding patterns in meaningless noise.

You know.

Pareidolia.

posts.content_html_raw:
Here's some assorted observations on 0.45 which I don't think have been pointed out yet. I'm planning on writing dedicated posts on the narrators, HOPE, and psycho Ami, so I mostly don't talk about those here.

First, here's a couple of favorite moments beyond what others have posted:

As usual, Ayane is hilarious. This Maya mostly shares Maya Prime's personality, but she seems a lot more relaxed. I imagine it was very stressful for Maya Prime to realize that she had finally found the "real" Akira and just one wrong move could doom her to another eternity of waiting.

This is such a great summary of Ayane's character, constantly pushing herself to move forward and put on a brave face for the benefit of others, even though it sometimes causes her to bottle up her own insecurities and doubts.
Now on to the lore. I tried to roughly order these from most to least interesting, at least for me, so feel free to stop reading when you reach the point of "Why is he wasting my time with this minor bullshit?"
Right before the new HOPE appears, there is a long sequence of flashing images. These are all images from old events with one exception (or maybe more, I didn't check super carefully). This image is completely new:
God of Spiders is surely Pareidolia. God of Love could maybe be HOPE, but he seems more like a God of Lust. In any case, this image appearing right before HOPE's return, as well as the "nyaa" connection with the angels, is one of the many reasons that I think Pareidolia is involved (more on that in a dedicated post). It also seems to suggest a Pareidolia connection to The Waiting Room and Giuseppe.
When Yumi meets Kaori in the alternate timeline, Kaori calls her Friend with a capital F. In the main timeline, I'm pretty sure Kaori has never used that name for anyone other than Sensei.
I'm really curious who this Kaori is. She's lit by a red glow but doesn't have SeKaori's eyes, so maybe that's supposed to represent Pareidolia, and of course Pareidolia knows Yumi by another name - probably not Friend, but they could have a prior relationship.

In addition, it's possible that Kaori shouldn't exist in this timeline. It's far from confirmed, but I think that Kaori was killed in the car crash and someone only altered the past to have her survive for the current cycle of the main timeline. Her presence (with her Sekai organs) is one the few things that makes this cycle special.

The narration is also concerning. I can't imagine that the narrator is just wrong and nothing bad happened to Yumi.
I don't know if it's important who this narrator is, but the reference to Yumi's goosebumps is a callback to events that I think are narrated by Tsubasa.
What did happen to Yumi is a mystery, but I wonder if HOPE gives us a clue on the roof.
I'm pretty sure this refers to Sana, who seemed to be somehow key to SekaiDolia's plan for a New Hope, but ended up rejecting them in her TSS. Yumi's "removal" happened right before HOPE was able to return. Did Kaori do something with her that brought HOPE back? Sana's role seemed to involve having sex with a god, would Sel really pull off-screen supernatural NTR?

One last thing to point out tangentially related to this: Alt Maya Prime is told that a reset is coming that she can't feel and decides to go off to do something. At the same time, she's also told that Yumi has a cousin named Kaori who knows about the resets and knows that one is coming. And yet, she doesn't seem to react to this information at all. Does this Maya know something about Kaori? Is that the actual reason she leaves? For now it's just a possibility to keep in mind for the future.
A character named youdidit shows up at the end of the new Untitled Children's Show, but we never actually see her. Maybe I'm crazy, but the way she talks sounds nothing like Long Maya to me.
It seems to me that something happened to Long Maya when she left to "feed herself to the Dark Entity" at the end her Sensei Quest appearance. Maybe Long Maya was destroyed and a new version was made by the clockwork?

Also possibly related: the hanging feet we see earlier in the show, maybe from someone doing a T-pose in midair.
I'm sure these could belong to any number of characters, but they look consistent with Maya to me. Any feet experts want to chime in?
In the new "Episcopalis", Sensei is addressing one of Sekai or Maya while comparing her to the other.

It's a bit confusing because they both wear ribbons. I think he's addressing Maya because Sekai (the kite with the key) is the original while Maya (the lightning rod) is the updated version. On the other hand, Maya is the smaller one, so I'm not sure.
The part I'm interested in is the idea that the addressee "returned herself". If it's Maya, is Sensei suggesting that Maya Prime deliberately sacrificed herself on the roof? Or is this another clue that Maya killed herself at some point in the past? If it's Sekai, we know Sensei blames her for leaving him, but does he really think she died deliberately?

There's another hint at Maya suicide later in the update: in the middle of New Maya's string of visions, images flash on the screen saying "so many save slots", implying that the memories the visions are based on are coming from Maya's save slots. Halftone said that you can only become his follower and unlock your save slots if you kill yourself in extremely violent fashion.
In the psycho Ami timeline, she quotes a line about moving people forward that has previously been used by Maya and Tsubasa.

...

...

...
It's also worth noting that this line seems to be what snaps Sensei out of PTSD after the murder - maybe he remembers hearing it before.

I hypothesized before that Maya and Tsubasa both said this because they're both narrators, which fits with us now knowing Ami is a narrator. Another possibility: in this timeline Ami has been spending time around her mom's friend Tsubasa.
A narrator, probably Ami, says that she can't see inside of Maya's head.
This might support another part of my narrator Tsubasa theory: in "You & Me Against the World" the narrator describes what Touka and Tsukasa are thinking, but doesn't know Tsubasa's thoughts. My hypothesis was that the narrators know what characters are thinking, except for each other.
When Ayane and Yumi arrive on the school roof, the angels tell them that the ceiling and floor have swapped places.
Things turning upside down is what happens when you physically slip between worlds. This suggests to me that the RAS survive the resets by going to a new world. Another recent clue to this: on the beach, Himawari didn't know what Ayane meant by "resets", but in 0.44 when she played Otoha, she acknowledged the existence of a time loop. The reason she didn't know what a reset was is because that's not what's actually happening; they're actually traveling to a different plane.
In the waiting room, Arjuna says that his predecessor was a girl with pink hair.
I saw a couple of people suggest this is Noriko, but I don't know if someone would call Noriko a "small girl"; she's well above average height. I'll propose an alternative: the pink-haired girl from the upside down house, who is specifically described as small.
"Bye, Bye Boner":

"How to Make Love Stay":
If true, this probably means that the girls got sent to the upside down house after they were "reconfigured", whatever that involves.

While I'm on the subject, by process of elimination we think that the pink-haired girl is Ai Ariyoshi. On the AreYouHappyHere twitter, the girls are often referred to by only the first letter of their name. For example:
So possibly Ai is the "unknown a of this color [pink]" from Mother's Milk? Though it's not really the right pink for pink hair.
I have a few probably minor things about the New Maya scene in the school with Sensei. First, this scene doesn't seem to fit anywhere in the main timeline. Maya is wearing her second school uniform (which she never wears outside of school) that she got in Chapter 2 and has her winter hairstyle. By the time Maya got that uniform, Sensei had started wearing a dark t-shirt for winter, but here he has the white t-shirt from Chapter 1 and Chapter 4.
Second, there's a return of the black moon which I can't remember seeing since the pregnant Ayane plotline. Third, New Maya doesn't know who Takoyaki Man is (which makes sense because Kumon-mi is constantly changing and he probably didn't exist before the resets) but for some reason this Sensei does know him.
Obviously, all of these could just be because a previous cycle went differently from the main timeline. Alternatively, they could be hints that what we're seeing is fake.

spoilers.title: 9. New Maya box scene
spoilers.html:
I have a few probably minor things about the New Maya scene in the school with Sensei. First, this scene doesn't seem to fit anywhere in the main timeline. Maya is wearing her second school uniform (which she never wears outside of school) that she got in Chapter 2 and has her winter hairstyle. By the time Maya got that uniform, Sensei had started wearing a dark t-shirt for winter, but here he has the white t-shirt from Chapter 1 and Chapter 4.
Second, there's a return of the black moon which I can't remember seeing since the pregnant Ayane plotline. Third, New Maya doesn't know who Takoyaki Man is (which makes sense because Kumon-mi is constantly changing and he probably didn't exist before the resets) but for some reason this Sensei does know him.
Obviously, all of these could just be because a previous cycle went differently from the main timeline. Alternatively, they could be hints that what we're seeing is fake.

Well...
There was a few things I really tried to pay attention to, but with what we learned in the most recent updates, maybe the most glaring thing for me is to really take a close look at Ami.
And I must say, there is really zero signs that she would be this omnipresent being that has a wicked and twisted plan and who wants to manipulate the world into something else. I'm not saying it's not possible, but at least before the first reset, Ami seems very innocent (in comparison) and I didn't notice any hints of her being Prime Ami or having any extra knowledge. This might of course change in the future chapters.
However, one thing from the very beginning made me wonder. Where was the journal from? The one Akira allegedly just kept in his room prior to the very first reset. I feel like this has been addressed before, and there might be an explanation coming where Maya might have actually left it for him, similar to the notes on the board. But just in case it is not, that very entry here would simply not make sense:
View attachment 4230548 If this was written by pre-reset Akira, he would not actually think that, obviously. Unless he was so paranoid that he was even afraid someone might go through his personal notes at home and find evidence of him having an affair with a student. Come to think of it, I guess it could be in character? Still, feels like a convenient lie to basically hide the plot twist for later.
So the first time I played this game, it must have been somewhere around update 0.13 to 0.16 or something. I didn't actually quit after the first happy scene or anything else disturbing like apparently so many players do. Admittedly though this game gave me this unique uneasiness that was both fascinating but also distracting.

The thing is, playing through the beginning, it reminded me how different I approached it back then. Sure, it was quite clearly intended to be (or at least appear as) a harem parody of sorts, with some DDLC inspirations thrown in for the horror and shock factor. Big fucking whoop. It was still a porn game, so I played it to grind the lewd scenes and "conquer" the girls.
Characters like, for example, Chika or Ayane were great, since they were very open quickly and just really cute and likable. But in the end, I didn't really expect to care for them (much like Sensei then, who openly identified himself as a detached character anyway, especially during the first cycle).

But now, whenever a lewd scene is coming up, I feel like I'm watching a sex scene in a Tom Cruise movie with my parents. Like, whipping out my mole rat to that would straight up feel like I should be put into an asylum. Not that the scenes are not hot or anything per se. It's just that the added context makes me realize that now I am not playing it for any dumb sex scenes anymore, but for the plot. And getting turned on by intimate encounters and character growth just feels so dirty and degenerate to my now all of a sudden.

But I don't know, this might also just be me. And I'm not judging anyone reacting differently to it, I just wanted to highlight the difference in perspective I have apparently grown over the years, with how closely I follow every character's arcs and actually started to see them as people and not CGs to collect. How ironically fitting for the theme, well done Selly.
So I remember vividly that the last version I had before I paused the game for a long time was 0.21. I actually didn't even finish it, it must have been somewhere in Chapter 2, even before Touka and Yasu joined the class.
That fact turned out to be significant, since I just now found out that there has been a excessive revamp of chapter 1 with the 0.24 update, not only changing a lot of the events but also adding some, notably for example Ode to a Marsh Warbler. I thought I was going crazy, because while I wasn't really surprised to have forgotten a few of the stuff from when I played the game for the first time all those years ago, I was absolutely sure that some stuff just didn't go the way I saw it now, I had to cross check it with the wiki.
It also made me feel less like a big dumb dumb, since it explained some instances where discussions on here were about facts and scenes that I had in mind differently because of it.

Anyways, since the wiki for the Marshwarbler event didn't have the hexadecimal translation for the transition image in the scene, I went ahead and did it myself.
View attachment 4230620

Now I am pretty sure this is just Sel being an ass and insulting me for wasting my time to find answers or hints. But there's enough subtle details in the text where I could at least imagine there might still be some meaning to it.

First off, the background mentions the Daddy Daughter Dance. We now basically have the confirmation that Akira is most likely Ami's Dad, not sure if this was supposed to be some light foreshadowing. But there is also a single blue iris. Who else has a single blue iris? Sel's favourite character, Kaori.
And the text itself mentions a dying cat (cat always makes me think of Maya). But who knits curtains to keep away the shadows? And the rain makes me think of the rain king of course. Is this somehow related to the upside down house?

I am clearly too dumb for this and this probably means nothing. I just had to vent since it took me like 15 minutes to copy all those dumb hexadecimal numbers into the browser
Click to expand...
Regarding the last image, after I got to the point in the game where I decided Himawari was Akira's daughter I had assumed that image was added as foreshadowing for that. I think a few other Himawari related things were added/changed in the rework as well.

But what's kind interesting reading it now is it also seems to make reference to the "Rain King" and "Frog/pee boy" stuff. If it's not just a coincidence that's kind of insane.
"you are the one with rain. you are the one who bathes in their piss. go jerk off or something."




I think there is also a few more images with the blue eye in them. At least one anyway. This is the one I remember off the top of my head. Still not really sure what it means, but after the latest update I'm tempted to think it ties into what's going on with Ami somehow. But that could be some kind of recency bias. It is from a Kaori event (Run, Rabbit, Run) so perhaps like you said, it does have something to do with her aswell. Especially now that we know for sure she does have Sekai's heart, there could be some kind of through line between the 3 of them and whatever is going on now with Ami. Also It is a chapter 3 event could that have something to do with the 3 eyes. The one you posted is a chapter 1 event with 1 eye.

spoilers.title: Now to what really hit me by surprise the most...
spoilers.html:
So the first time I played this game, it must have been somewhere around update 0.13 to 0.16 or something. I didn't actually quit after the first happy scene or anything else disturbing like apparently so many players do. Admittedly though this game gave me this unique uneasiness that was both fascinating but also distracting.

The thing is, playing through the beginning, it reminded me how different I approached it back then. Sure, it was quite clearly intended to be (or at least appear as) a harem parody of sorts, with some DDLC inspirations thrown in for the horror and shock factor. Big fucking whoop. It was still a porn game, so I played it to grind the lewd scenes and "conquer" the girls.
Characters like, for example, Chika or Ayane were great, since they were very open quickly and just really cute and likable. But in the end, I didn't really expect to care for them (much like Sensei then, who openly identified himself as a detached character anyway, especially during the first cycle).

But now, whenever a lewd scene is coming up, I feel like I'm watching a sex scene in a Tom Cruise movie with my parents. Like, whipping out my mole rat to that would straight up feel like I should be put into an asylum. Not that the scenes are not hot or anything per se. It's just that the added context makes me realize that now I am not playing it for any dumb sex scenes anymore, but for the plot. And getting turned on by intimate encounters and character growth just feels so dirty and degenerate to my now all of a sudden.

But I don't know, this might also just be me. And I'm not judging anyone reacting differently to it, I just wanted to highlight the difference in perspective I have apparently grown over the years, with how closely I follow every character's arcs and actually started to see them as people and not CGs to collect. How ironically fitting for the theme, well done Selly.

spoilers.title: What I really wanted to bring up though:
spoilers.html:
So I remember vividly that the last version I had before I paused the game for a long time was 0.21. I actually didn't even finish it, it must have been somewhere in Chapter 2, even before Touka and Yasu joined the class.
That fact turned out to be significant, since I just now found out that there has been a excessive revamp of chapter 1 with the 0.24 update, not only changing a lot of the events but also adding some, notably for example Ode to a Marsh Warbler. I thought I was going crazy, because while I wasn't really surprised to have forgotten a few of the stuff from when I played the game for the first time all those years ago, I was absolutely sure that some stuff just didn't go the way I saw it now, I had to cross check it with the wiki.
It also made me feel less like a big dumb dumb, since it explained some instances where discussions on here were about facts and scenes that I had in mind differently because of it.

Anyways, since the wiki for the Marshwarbler event didn't have the hexadecimal translation for the transition image in the scene, I went ahead and did it myself.
View attachment 4230620

Now I am pretty sure this is just Sel being an ass and insulting me for wasting my time to find answers or hints. But there's enough subtle details in the text where I could at least imagine there might still be some meaning to it.

First off, the background mentions the Daddy Daughter Dance. We now basically have the confirmation that Akira is most likely Ami's Dad, not sure if this was supposed to be some light foreshadowing. But there is also a single blue iris. Who else has a single blue iris? Sel's favourite character, Kaori.
And the text itself mentions a dying cat (cat always makes me think of Maya). But who knits curtains to keep away the shadows? And the rain makes me think of the rain king of course. Is this somehow related to the upside down house?

I am clearly too dumb for this and this probably means nothing. I just had to vent since it took me like 15 minutes to copy all those dumb hexadecimal numbers into the browser

posts.content_html_raw:
Lux Perpetua said:
It amazes me how such an intelligent and smart person can be so shortsighted and greedy
Click to expand...
Creative types' view of online piracy is rarely... strategic. Or rational. I understand it from that side--I've made my living mostly through by sales of copyright-protected media. Watching stuff I'd spent hundreds or even thousands of hours on be freely shared without my consent? Maddening. Gut-wrenching. Enraging.

But a few of the things I learned very early on are:
  1. Piracy is inevitable
  2. Most pirates will never become paying readers/viewers/listeners/players--though (as this thread shows) they can become vocal fans
  3. DRM is completely useless, and just makes your fans/supporters grumpy*
  4. Most "piracy" sites on the internet never actually have any stolen content; they're just honey traps for stealing personal info, getting credit card numbers off the unsuspecting, and installing trojan horses to scrape more info, launch DDoS attacks, and other fun things
  5. The best way to combat piracy is to make your work easily available in as many formats on the retail sites people are used to getting their [whatever] from so that those folks who do want to pay can do so
  6. Since [1], [2], and [3], it's best to look at sites like this (and, say, ScribD, etc.) as marketing opportunities
Most creators (ie, Selebus) can't get past the gut rage at feeling their precious (and I'm using that word unironically) work is being stolen. I get that, but hey. Deal with the world as it is, so you can move it in the direction of the world you want it to be.

* DRM is actually only useful as a way for retailers to silo customers into their ecosystem--so you can't read your Kobo ebook on Apple Books, say, or listen to your Nook audiobook on a Kindle. It's expensive (either in money or time). It's easily broken. So, yeah. From a creator's point of view, useless.

posts.content_html_raw:
I think we have already agreed on several occasions that Sel's idea of gameplay is pretty bad, and he might not even necessarily disagree with the general notion that the gameplay experience could be better.

But calling it unplayable is simply unfair and untrue, both on the factual level as well as the perceived one.
It's repetitive and can sometimes feel unfair in how complicated some of the unlock conditions are for certain events, but it's definitely manageable, at least many on here did so without abandoning it.
And while I would generally agree that the gameplay can be off-putting for some players, I think the main reasons for people abandoning it are usually other ones.

However, I want to remind people that the general consensus here is that going the green route and seeing all events is the one true way to play the game as it is the author's vision and "canon". That does make sense and I can get behind that, but at the end of the day, it is up to the players to decide whether they want to do it the way the author intended or make use of other options available and risk skipping content.

Virtually the same can be said about the general gameplay loop. Sel's vision probably would be for the player to feel some form of frustration by having to figure out the correct sequence of events or finding happy scenes seemingly by random. I think the Alexis happy scene is a good recent example for this. Even potentially missing events if you fail to follow the "correct" choices gives a bit of meaning and reason for this being called a game as opposed to a kinetic novel.
However, understandably, some players want to ignore that vision and do it their way and use the guide mod to get through the game faster and without worrying to miss anything.

Personally, I haven't used the guide mod in the past, I have worked through the grind and reputative gameplay loop, knowing it will reward me with good content. I also haven't followed the green route, making decisions based on personal preferences and an interpretation of what an authentic choice for Akira would be, even if it means missing scenes.
That being said, I am glad the mod exists and have started using it during my current replay, mostly to make sure I get to see all events.

I want to stress however that there is one clear exception to all of this where I cannot possibly defend Sel:
The reset puzzles are ass and should be reworked, at least in the future. Those I am pretty sure have frustrated some of the new players enough to drop this title.
I also belong to the group of people who had to look up here or on reddit for puzzle solutions, since the experience is nowhere as fulfilling or clever as Sel probably thinks it is.
Like honestly, just make it lore-based questions or something, the girls favorite stuff or anything that would be somewhat fun to look up if you are not called aramaug, Moonflare or Deskel and know it by heart. Just not random sequences of numbers that were hidden in the corner of an obscure event or stuff you literally need to google. Or trial & error clicking things until something happens. Bad! Bad Selebus!

It's all good, misunderstandings happen.
I kind of get the notion of the content being a little "too much" sometimes. There really is a lot of words. During my first playthrough, at least in the beginning, I had phases where I skipped parts of content I was not particularly interested in.
Once you really get into it though I found it hard to just skip and enjoyed even the little conversations between characters I initially didn't like that much. I remember that I had favorites in the beginning of the game that I wanted to speedrun their content first. And that once the class expanded that I disliked most of the new students, only for them to grow on me to the point where I like some of them more than most of the initial ten.

And yeah, you can essentially always cut a lot of dialogue while still having the plot makes sense and be coherent. But one of the main things dialogue does is it builds character development and background.
Sure, you don't need to read the conversations Akira has with Io in the onsen about baseball or about how Io is a depressive wreck but appreciates Akira, and what Akira thinks of all that. But it establishes a certain bond, you feel like the characters are growing closer and understand each other with every shared conversation. Which in turn amplifies the impact of a decision during a fateful future scene (which, again, I haven't even watched yet and am dreading to get to during my replay).

This is just an example of many where dialogue provides further nuance and gives the general plot movements more meaning and solidifies character relationships.

What I would generally recommend to newer players, as counterintuitive as it may seem, is to look at this game less like a NSFW porn game to jerk off to, but to treat it like a book that you want to read through during some quiet time. Take your time to pay attention and let it all sink in and enjoy the intimate moments as a sort of extra if you will, but not treat them as a motivation to skim through the "main" content.

And regarding the Jesus comment, I feel like there have been so many Jesus pictures and mentions that I'm afraid you'd have to be more specific and show me the scene/screenshot that you are referring to in order to better understand your stance.

PS: I think it is fair to assume that anyone that posts here is up-to-date on the latest update. Content/development that has been specifically revealed during the last update are generally but into spoiler tags either in-line (like this) or as a separate spoiler box (see below) for at least the first few days after it came out, probably up until the public release? I don't think there is a hard rule here.

posts.content_html_raw:
shmurfer said:
Has Selebus ever put out any sort of hint that he doesn't like the Guide mod? I've seen people mention being scared of URM'ing the game but the guide mod adds its own flags that should be easy enough to detect.
Click to expand...
I think some people overestimate both what one is capable of doing from a Renpy build and what Selebus "the programmer" is able to do. Not directed to you, but I'd like to share some thoughts on the topic since it's been brought up.
Being scared of using URM makes no sense unless one is ignorant of what URM is. It is a mod that enables you to alter flags and jump to events manually, being able to alter flags means that whatever flags for cheating, or whatever Selebus makes, you can just turn off with one click. The shampoo situation where Selebus delights on trolling his own supporters? you can just turn that off. It also allows you to see multiple variations of events during normal play by just rolling back and changing the flag for say "stomachache on" or "off". Finally, people brought up the "I need a save from the Amy event because I'm afraid of triggering it through URM", that's just ignorance. The game is unable to see the difference from triggering through URM because a manual trigger through URM puts you in that moment of the game and lets you play it from there, it's exactly like loading a save (you can do it for any event at any time).

What Selebus is able to do is insert a DRM that deletes your saves, which he has already done with catastrophic consequences to people's good faith in him. So, if someone is afraid, simply back up your saves before playing a leaked update - that's the most he can do. He won't resort to malware, and anything that would "break your game" you can just turn off with URM. Mind you, Selebus breaks the game of regular users anyway (like the shampoo situation) because who'd question his artistic vision.

Regarding the guide mod, it's only updated as the official version comes out, so it's unlikely Selebus is at odds with it. The author goes out of his way to wait for the official release in order to release it - even though that makes little sense to me either. The guide mod can be used by a Selebus supporter without any leaked version, but anyway... I, or one of the regulars, would probably be faster in providing triggers anyway - so it doesn't really matter in the long run if the guide mod takes a while to update.
Advice is the same as always: Install URM, always update the guide mod if you're going to replay, always backup your saves before playing the next update, completely disregard Selebus' antics and if something comes up, we'll simply tell you what to do (as we do for triggers and puzzles).

So first, a little context:

I downloaded 0.23 of LiL on Sel's Subscribestar, because I know this is the last version before he reworked a lot of Chapter 1. Entire events were deleted or altered. Because of this, I thought I'd look at the deleted content since I'm replaying the game anyways.

Anyway, as I looked through the files to see what was different, I noticed this:

THE ORIGINAL CHAPTER 2 COVER GIRL WAS YUMI???



Maybe some of you on here remember it, but to me this was kinda mindblowing. I'm so used to seeing Maya there, which I suppose in hindsight makes more sense. Still, I wonder what Sel's original intent was there...

The whole beginning of the game is completely different so far, so I'm curious to see how it holds up.

Alas, this is a take and not character stats so I am less inclined to put all the eggs into the same basket, even if the basket is my own headcannon.

There are animations, but they do not appear in story scenes.

Whenever an act is unlocked with a girl, it may create a repeatable animated scene. For example -- in the screenshot I included, "Hang Out" would potentially trigger a story scene, if one is available, or a static scene in which Affection is raised if a story scene isn't available, but the "Have sex" options are all animations.

There are animations available at the dorms, when you invite girls over via phone, or when you visit some of the girls at their hangout/work (Maki at the sex shop, Sara at the bar, Haruka at the coffee shop, etc).

Some animations may become unavailable for story reasons in certain parts of the game.

Well this is weird as shit. The images appear to contain hidden data that (I think) was placed there deliberately, but most of it is meaningless.

amisroomonefive25.webp was still normal in 0.39. Starting with 0.40, each full game version includes a new version of the image with different corruption. The data in the files is identical except for one block starting at offset 0x8000 that is exactly 0x1000 bytes (4KiB) long.

The modified bytes in the 0.40 image themselves contain an image file, specifically a tiny jpeg showing Singapore's ArtScience Museum. This is smaller than the 4KiB block, the rest of which is padded with zeros.

Why does Sekai hates being called Ms. Arakawa? Is it because it makes her remember nozomu? Or her original last name so important to her that being a Arakawa is a downgrade?
Click to expand...
Sekai hates her previous name, which would be Sekai Miyahara. She chooses not to answer anyone that calls her Miyahara, per Karin's dad testimony. Other than that, Sekai would also naturally be an Arakawa by birth (being Yuu's daughter with Miu), just not by name.
Her disliking being called Ms. Arakawa would likely be because of Nozomu, but could be overall because she hates the name to begin with since it comes from Yuu, which likely left her mom for Saki, or something happened that she was unable to have his name since birth.
In the timeline that she marries Akira, she would have been Ms. Arakawa by marriage to Nozomu before, so maybe it makes her remember bad memories (as she was being abused at the time). Deep theorizing aside, the simplest theory would be that it makes her feel old, useful to remember that she's more or less 10 years older than Akira, so by the time that the timetravel happens, Akira would be 30 and she'd be around 40.

posts.content_html_raw: It seems like we're largely skeptical of Pareidolia's claim of both benevolence and subsequent banishment to the bottom of the well. I admit I took its claims at face value and assumed it would exit the narrative, but I likewise see the value in the perspective of its unity with HOPE. Any strong opinions on this particular god's place in the narrative moving forward?

posts.content_html_raw:
CovertCobalt said:
It seems like we're largely skeptical of Pareidolia's claim of both benevolence and subsequent banishment to the bottom of the well. I admit I took its claims at face value and assumed it would exit the narrative, but I likewise see the value in the perspective of its unity with HOPE. Any strong opinions on this particular god's place in the narrative moving forward?
Click to expand...
short answer: we'll have to wait and see.

longer answer: I don't think Pareidolia is outright lying, even if he's lying.We have seen proof that gods are bound to their legends, and he is the concerned god. He has been dragged from the well by Akira when he was a kid, and provided for Akira "concern" since then. So even if he is lying, it would still be out of concern. It is highly unlikely that Pareidolia is "dead", as even during his sacrifice he makes mention of leaving gifts scattered through the timeline and that "when they next meet, he hopes they'll be able to harmonize better" or some such. Pareidolia is definitely taking his biggest gamble there (by sacrificing himself), including sending our Nodoka as one of the gifts to "move Akira", that ultimately led to her sacrifice in order for Akira to learn that Ami is a psychopath (among other things).

just plain long answer: We still don't know enough about the nature of the gods, what we do know now, although helpful, complicated things further. There are millions of gods, and they are born and vanish without much notice (which is a very real take on the eastern approach to gods anyway). Pray to the moon enough and you might summon a moon god, same for air, same for chair, same for anything really. Forget about them, and it's down to the bottom of the well, and eventual manifestation as a human, or worse. The way this complicates things is because we still don't know if the four gods are of the same group as these or not. Are HOPE, Wires, Pareidolia and USER4 gods that just happened to get to this cycle first? (or are they something different, as Akira is called the child of makeshift gods, maybe these gods aren't even real gods in the first place). Is the myth of the four that were one just a way to interpret the notion that the Kaori (or a similar hotel) at the time had four slots to be filled and they were the first in? Without proper understanding of this, it becomes hard for us to properly distinguish between HOPE the peerless god of light coming back with "3"s around him just after Pareidolia's gone (which is USER3) being their union, or another random thing thrown out there.

Okay, I'm tired of writing. Pareidolia, teleport me back home. Or to Molly's house... Actually, teleport me and Molly to a cosplay store instead.

(praise Pareidolia, our one true bro and uber service)
